entries.implementationStatus: not-yet-implemented as a registered adapter: the adapter is gap G2 of docs/polaris-generation/TRACKER.md and sits on an unmerged branch (PR #258 at the time of drafting). This version is a candidate for the owner to read, not a usable entry: RFC4-3 admits no output from an entry whose implementationVersion is Unknown, so a later version carrying the implementation version and the pinned governing contract version replaces this one through its own review and act. implementationVersion stays null (Unknown), never a placeholder
entries.contractVersionSource: the value the adopted Butlers observer entry declares for the same contract; re-derive by script before the offering

governingBehaviorContract.version: Unknown: pinned by the offering step to the generation specification bytes in force, base REQ-polaris-generation-017 plus the understanding and tree-form amendments
governingBehaviorContract.signedBy: pending exact owner act over this entry

entries.authorizationModeDerivation: the entry needs an effective exact owner act (RFC3-16(a)) and the effective egress consent for the (project:syzygy, provider:anthropic) pair; owner-trusted-bootstrap while those acts are state (1); every other combination dispatches nothing
entries.provenanceDisclosure: The route is admitted on owner-trusted records; independent audit is not configured.

inputClasses.identityScheme: not-recorded: the credential's presence is a precondition, its value and identity are never written to a record

entries.determinism: every output is a recording of what the provider returned at a capture instant; a re-dispatch may legitimately differ. The generated prose is editorial inference, never an Observed claim and never repeatable by contract

typedAuthority.authorityTypeLabel: [Inferred] a provider is an external authority of project:syzygy under RFC4-1; the typed-authority list in the RFC names version control, hosting, the scheduler and the OpenSpec CLI as examples, so this type name is the drafter's
questions: What did the provider return for this exact request?
typedAuthority.readAuthority: none: the route reads no source. It transmits the request the generator built (the stage system prompt and the stage input envelope, each after the single egress check, RFC5-15) together with the bytes the pinned runtime adds itself, and receives the reply. [Observed, capture endpoint, no provider contacted] the additions are listed in full in requestBytes: a fixed system prefix, an empty system message carrying the pinned effort, metadata.user_id with a random per-run-directory device id and session id, stream, cache_control on the generator's parts, the pinned model, the max_tokens ceiling, the headers listed there (including the platform headers that identify the machine's OS, CPU architecture and Node runtime version) and, after some failures, a body-less HEAD /api/hello probe
typedAuthority.runDirectoryWrites: provider requests, replies, run records and the runtime's own state, including any session transcript, are written inside the run directory under project:syzygy's state directory, outside git, from the start of the run (the egress record's retention line). [Unknown] whether a signed-in runtime refreshes or writes its credential outside that directory; the entry cannot be offered until that is checked
networkAccess: the Anthropic API host, through the Claude Agent SDK runtime, signed in with the owner's account or key; the connectivity probe HEAD /api/hello goes to the same host and carries no generator bytes; no other destination
typedAuthority.generatorBuiltContent: exactly two request parts are generator content: the stage system prompt and the stage input envelope (the user text block), each carrying the cache_control the runtime attaches. Everything else in the request is listed in requestBytes as runtime-fixed or pinned by this entry and carries no source span
typedAuthority.writeSurfaceArgument: writeSurface is empty because nothing is written to the observed repository, its forks, its tracker or any Anthropic-hosted object the owner could later edit. The dispatch itself is an effect (the pipeline rechecks effect permission immediately before it); the egress consent is the explicit authority for that effect and for the provider's retention under the account's terms, which this entry does not widen
typedAuthority.toolInvocationNote: the empty list holds in the default text mode. The opt-in schema mode adds exactly one tool, StructuredOutput, which contradicts no-tools; it is off by default and enabling it is a different route condition that the egress record must name first

routeConditions.source: record PUBLIC-EGRESS-anthropic of the public-repo admission package (PR #215), version 0.1.0-candidate.7 at drafting. A version string does not identify bytes (the record kept that version across edits), so the offering step pins the record by the digest of its own manifest row. The egress record is the authority; this block only declares what the implementation will enforce and cannot widen it
routeConditions.tools: tools is [] in the request; no tool of the runtime or the provider's side is offered or invoked; the opt-in StructuredOutput schema mode is off by default (see toolInvocationNote)
routeConditions.ambientContext: the runtime loads no instruction or memory files, user or project settings, MCP servers, hooks, environment summary or safeguards block; its working directory is an empty directory inside the run directory. The runtime-fixed system prefix and empty system message are model-visible context the generator did not build; they are listed in requestBytes. The egress record's Conditions say the route adds no context of its own, so accepting this envelope needs an egress record version that admits the listed runtime-fixed bytes (packet O4)
routeConditions.telemetry: telemetry, error reporting and update checks are disabled; a run whose runtime cannot disable them does not start
routeConditions.stateLocation: a run whose runtime cannot keep its state and transcript inside the run directory does not start
routeConditions.acceptanceCheck: the adapter is accepted only when a request captured at a local endpoint, before any real call, shows (1) the generator-built parts byte for byte equal to what the generator built and (2) every other byte equal to requestBytes: the runtimeFixed list, the routeFixedByThisEntry values, the headers list and the probe, for the pinned SDK and CLI versions. Any byte, header or field in neither fails. The check separates runtime envelope from content and admits no profile-set byte beyond the values this entry pins
routeConditions.fallback: none: a failure never routes to another provider, to the direct API or to a tool

portMapping.note: [Observed] the ports exist; [Unknown] how the runtime reports usage, a model identifier and late receipts, so usage fields are Unknown (Missing quantity) rather than zero when unreported

unknowns: whether the Agent SDK on a subscription login can meet the route conditions (gap #21); with an API key it is [Unknown] too; the entry cannot be offered for the first real call until this is checked
[Unknown] whether the real API accepts the empty system message with the effort setting: only a capture endpoint has seen it
[Unknown] traffic on paths the capture did not take: error handling beyond 429 and 529, long runs and login flows
whether a signed-in runtime writes or refreshes its credential outside the run directory
the runtime's context window and rate limits
the provider's own retention under the terms and settings of the account or key used, which the egress record discloses and does not promise

runtimeCannotMeetRouteConditions.note: an environment the profile could not satisfy (RFC2-24 reason 12); not an observer error, and no degradation state is invented

usageUncertain.note: the pipeline stops with usage-uncertain; absent tokens or cost are Unknown, never zero (RFC2-23). RFC2-23 names no reason for Missing quantity: unreported usage is an absent evidence quantity for a cost claim, which is reason 2 rather than an uncaptured deterministic input (reason 10) [Inferred]

failureStates.dispatchUncertain: not a degradation state: an execution fact (the pipeline stops with effect-uncertain and a lease expiry never replays the request), routed through the existing claim-reason predicate like budget exhaustion (ADAPTER-DECLARATIONS.md, failure behaviour)
failureStates.budgetExhaustedOrRejectedOutput: not a degradation state: distinct execution facts (ADAPTER-DECLARATIONS.md, failure behaviour), mapped to the existing claim-reason predicate

adapterFailureAtReachableEndpoint.note: a malformed stream or a 5xx from a reachable endpoint is an adapter error (RFC4-4), distinct from routeUnreachable

failureStates.cancelledOrDeadline: not a degradation state: execution facts like budget exhaustion (the pipeline stops with cancelled or deadline), routed through the existing claim-reason predicate

admissionFailureMapping.missingConsent: unconsented-source-or-provider (a refused effect under the permission predicate; no withdrawal event is invented)

entries.supersession: signing these bytes would register the route's declared boundary and enable nothing; a usable entry is a later observerVersion that fills implementationVersion and governingBehaviorContract.version, is reviewed afresh and is signed by its own act (rule 10: any byte change retires this row)
entries.routeSubstitution: RFC4-1 allows exactly one registered adapter per external authority per project. A different route to Anthropic (for example the Messages API route, PR #264) is a substitute that replaces this entry by a successor version or entry under a new act; it never runs beside this one and this entry never falls back to it

runtimePin.note: [Inferred] per PROVIDER-EGRESS-BYTES.md (PR #258): the adapter is designed to refuse construction on another SDK version and to fail a call whose CLI announces another; the adapter is unmerged and a bump is a new entry version

snapshotInputMapping.label: [Inferred] RFC2-1 items; the installed Butlers entry carries no mapping, so the gap is inherited and this mapping is the drafter's
snapshotInputMapping.admitted-source-bundle: item 8 (deterministic configuration affecting classification) and item 1 for the admitted revisions it was drawn from
snapshotInputMapping.owner-sign-in-credential: none: never recorded (its presence is a precondition, not a snapshot input)
snapshotInputMapping.outputs: provider-reply-capture, usage-record, dispatch-evidence and model-identity are item 6

requestBytes.status: the exact request the route may carry for the pinned versions, inline so the bytes an act binds are these bytes; PROVIDER-EGRESS-BYTES.md is cited as provenance only and its later edits change nothing here
requestBytes.provenance: [Observed, capture endpoint, no provider contacted] PROVIDER-EGRESS-BYTES.md on the branch of PR #258, blob 2e7d176e668417bf9842be8b11703f5fe2cc39ca at commit 420c60f91a7122cc0224a29ec41d4e9bb29d5ec8; that adapter is unmerged
generatorBuilt: system[1]: exactly the stage system prompt, with cache_control ephemeral attached to it
messages[0]: one user text block, exactly the stage input envelope, with cache_control ephemeral attached to it
runtimeFixed: system[0]: You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK. (cache_control ephemeral)
metadata.user_id: {"device_id":"<hex64>","account_uuid":"","session_id":"<uuid>"}, both ids random per run directory

routeFixedByThisEntry.thinking: absent (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_THINKING=1); enabling it adds thinking and context_management and is not a permitted configuration
routeFixedByThisEntry.maxTokensCeiling: [Inferred proposal] 32000; the sent max_tokens is the minimum of this ceiling, the profile's maxOutputTokens and the dispatch permit's output and usage allowances, so the permit may only lower it
routeFixedByThisEntry.note: model, tools, effort and max_tokens are profile-set in the measurement; this entry pins them so they are bytes it lists as fixed, the form the egress record admits

requestBytes.headerNote: the x-stainless platform headers identify the machine's OS, CPU architecture and Node runtime version
requestBytes.probe: after some failures the CLI sends HEAD /api/hello with user-agent Bun/1.4.3 and no body to the API host; it carries no generator bytes and is the only non-message request allowed
absentByConstruction: any tool, including StructuredOutput (schema mode is off by default)
requestBytes.unlistedBytes: any byte, header or field not listed above fails the acceptance check

entries.determinismClassNote: the scalar form is kept for the shape precedent's key and names the primary class; determinismByOutputClass is the machine form and governs
